options.text: Evolve contracts additively across a compatibility window and retire old behavior only with evidence. In this transfer case for partner webhook delivery, readers and writers must coexist; schema and api compatibility are operational constraints. The owner must also make a receiver that acknowledges late observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide api versioning and backward compatibility independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a receiver that acknowledges late as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Evolve contracts additively across a compatibility window and retire old behavior only with evidence. It addresses the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates through an explicit mechanism and keeps a receiver that acknowledges late inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Readers and writers must coexist; schema and API compatibility are operational constraints. The transfer case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For partner webhook delivery, the decision keeps the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a receiver that acknowledges late as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “API versioning and backward compatibility” to terminology recall. Distinguish protocol mechanics from domain boundaries; a fashionable API style is not automatically the correct contract. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce api versioning and backward compatibility must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unowned_shortcut: It leaves api versioning and backward compatibility dependent on caller discipline instead of placing the decision with the boundary that can enforce it.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unbounded_scale: The extra mechanism may change consistency, duplicate work, or recovery behavior without addressing the decisive requirement.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.ignore_failure: A design answer must state what the user sees and who owns recovery when a receiver that acknowledges late occurs.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.provider_trivia: The architecture decision should survive a provider change; the mechanism and contract matter more than a product label.
